# Testing

- TST-004: Coverage gates: 100% line coverage for pure domain assemblies, 95% for application assemblies, 90% overall; mutation score 85% (nightly).
- TST-010: Unit tests follow Microsoft's unit-testing best practices. Name each test for the method, the scenario and the expected behavior. Try to include only one Act task per test. Avoid logic in a test (string concatenation, if, while, for, switch) and avoid magic strings. Keep a test's input to the simplest information needed. Try not to introduce infrastructure dependencies into unit tests; reserve them for integration tests. Create the objects a test needs in the test or in a helper method, in preference to Setup and Teardown attributes when tests have different setup requirements; where every test needs the same initialization, per-test setup is appropriate, and for synchronous initialization prefer the constructor. In most cases don't test a private method: test the public method that calls it. Where production code calls a static reference such as DateTime.Now, introduce a seam so the test has full control.
- TST-011: The kit's additions to its unit tests, beyond Microsoft's best practices (TST-010): write each test name as the method, the scenario and the expected behavior without underscores (AddRejectsAMissingRequestByName); arrange, act and assert; keep try out of a test; and bring time, randomness and other outside state in through seams such as TimeProvider.
